items.titleEn: Every word of Renée’s and Alessia’s pre-Benfica presser
items.summaryEn: Slegers and Russo sat down at the Sobha Realty Training Centre on Tuesday for their pre-Benfica press conference
bodyEn: Renée Slegers and Alessia Russo sat down in front of the media at the Sobha Realty Training Centre on Tuesday for their pre-Benfica press conference.
The pair looked ahead to Wednesday's UEFA Women's Champions League clash at Meadow Park in Borehamwood.
Here's everything they had to say on the following subjects...

on the last couple of days since the north London derby:RS: It's been good. Players and staff had the day off the day after. And I think you could see in the celebrations after the game how good that was for us and the energy it created. We've come back in, so it's been the balance of recovering post-game and then getting ready for the Benfica game tomorrow, of course. And there's been great energy.

on enjoying the penalty and celebrations:AR: Yeah, it was really nice. I think you could see in how we played in the game, but also how we celebrated at the end that it meant a lot to win the north London derby. It means a lot to the club, to us players and staff. So, yeah, it felt really nice to get that win and we hope now that it can build momentum going into these next few games.
on Reid’s and Agyemang’s injuries:RS: They're not back yet, and it's the same as for the last game. Frida's progressing well too, but tomorrow will come too soon. Kim Little is back in the squad.
on if Katie is struggling:RS: We'll see. She's, of course, coming back from a long-term injury. So hopefully everything's okay and we'll do some assessment.

on if Catley and Hinds playing together is a long-term solution:RS: I think they did incredibly well in the game. I think it played out the way we wanted it to, and credit to the players on the pitch for getting it so right and doing their role with so much conviction and quality. So I think the left side in particular had a really good game, but us as a collective, I think the way we play with intensity, with fight in the game, with the grittiness that is necessary in a north London derby, that's for us the foundation. In the performances going forward as well. There were some really good things, but now we have to back it up and the next one's tomorrow.

on if our overall mood has changed with the clocks changing, and if we’re block by block rather than game by game:RS: Game by game still. I think my kids haven't gotten used to the change of clocks yet! It was raining, by the way, this morning. It was lovely and sunny when we were out on the training pitch. No, we stick with game by game. It's important for us. We don't look too far ahead. We're very excited for the Champions League game tomorrow. Excited to be back close with the fans at Meadow Park and play under the lights. I know what it means for the players to play in the Champions League, so game by game, and the next one is Benfica.

on if playing against Spurs is good practice for Benfica:RS: There are some similarities we expect. I think the amount of duelling in the north London derby, the physicality on the pitch, the intensity that was necessary in the battle on the pitch, we expect the same tomorrow. They're a very robust team with a good organisation, good structures, and they fight. So, in that sense, we expect to face something similar. The good thing is that we did that well in the game on the weekend, and we want to go to the next level with it.

on the Ballon d’Or:AR: Yeah, it was really nice. I think it's special to celebrate people's seasons and bring the football world together. It was nice to go with Mariona. Yeah, I think it's a moment where you can enjoy the highs and lows of football. I think it was a special night to see, obviously, Harry Kane win. I was so excited about that. I think he's one of my role models growing up, and I think as soon as he got announced, I had goosebumps. Obviously, Alexia [Putellas] is an incredible player as well, so I think it was really nice to celebrate their individual moments. Then I also think it gives you some motivation to want to kick on. I know what we want to achieve as a team this year, and maybe it's been tough to begin with, but I believe that we've still got great things ahead in this team and this season.

on if she pushes through blips in form like Kane:AR: I mean, it's an honour to say that I'm anything like Harry Kane, but I think that I definitely try and learn off him. I think he's an incredible leader and player. I love how he drops a bit deeper, he gets on the ends of crosses, he finds half a yard to shoot, he's good off both feet. So, yeah, I think if there's anyone's game that I could try and learn from, it would be his.

on if we’ve had to be grittier in our mentality this season:AR: 100 per cent. I think you always learn different things throughout seasons. You pose different challenges, and I think, yeah, you have to dig deep. I think, for sure, times have been a little bit tougher, but we've got a resilient squad, resilient people around us, and I think sometimes tough moments bring out really great things from teams, and I hope that's what we're going to go on to do this season as well.

on what we want to see more of after the win against Spurs:RS: Yeah, so like I just said, the foundation for us in the win was the intensity that we brought to the game, us as a collective attacking and defending together, the fight, the grittiness, the resilience, because also they scored the first goal in the game and we have to come back from it. So those things are important for us, and we definitely want to bring that to tomorrow night's game as well. I think the goal that we scored, Alessia sets up the opportunity for Georgia, how we make several deep runs, I think it's the third or the fourth run that we break the line with, and then we have so much composure to set up a player forward facing and to get a finish off. That was really positive and something we've been working on talking about. So if we can do that more often and bring that even more to games consistently, we know the quality in the squad. But yeah, the foundation was definitely in the grittiness and the fight.

on if there’s more of an emphasis now on success in the Champions League:RS: Even though the start has been tough for us and there's been results that we aren't happy with, I still think it's too early to say because there's so much to play for still in the league as well. So like I just said, it's game by game and we're very proud to be part of the Champions League again. It's a fantastic stage and that's what we're focused on so Benfica tomorrow.

on how we approach coming up against Benfica tactically:RS: They have their identity, of course. Remember the game from last year that we played there away,t hey made it hard for us, we ended up winning 2-0. They've played their two games against Juventus and Bayern. They compete and we know that they will compete against us tomorrow as well. So there will be some similarities. They have their identity, a really robust, compact structure in the league. They've had an amazing run since 2024, I think. So there's a lot of similarities based on the last game we played against them but they do something slightly different. Some personnel is different as well.

on how to reset after missing a big opportunity as a striker:AR: First and foremost, I think it's about training. We train a lot on finishing moments, penalties as well. So I think whenever the moment comes, you know that you've done the work in the week and that's something that gives me confidence. Also, I think that's just how football goes. I think as a striker, as a forward, you know you're going to get chances and it's about doing as well as you can. I felt like it was a good contact, it was a good save [from Lize Kop early in the second half]. I didn't feel too much pressure going into the penalty. Obviously, I knew I wanted to score for the club for what it meant in that moment but you train for these moments all the time, so it trains you to be ready for them in the moments.

on if we can take anything from last season’s 2-0 win away to Benfica:AR: Yes, I mean like Renée said, we know they're a really tough side to break down. We saw that when we played them away. We saw that when they played Bayern, they didn't score until late on in the game and I think it doesn't matter when we score. Of course, we'd love to score in the first couple of minutes but sometimes football doesn't work like that. So we're prepared, we'll do everything we can to break them down as early as possible but we know they have threats and we have to be aware of that too. So yes, we're confident going into the game but whether it comes in the first minute or the last minute, we're focused on the win no matter how.

on what she does as a leader in difficult moments:AR: We have a squad full of young talent but also really experienced professionals that have been at the top of the game for a long time and I feel like I'm slowly edging towards that, so there is a responsibility on me to step up a little bit more. I think the way I lead is by how I train and what I give on the pitch. That's something that I commit to every day. But also, I'm quite a positive, laid-back person, so I think sometimes that can help the younger players when there is a lot of pressure on results and there are hard times. Maybe I think I can try and relieve some of their stress, which is something that I would pride myself on. I'm still learning as a leader. I have great people to look up to. I think that I try and help them as much as I can by being myself and authentic to me and hopefully I can continue to grow in that role as well.

on Cooney-Cross’ form this season:AR: The Kyra that I signed with four years ago to now is a completely different person and player. I think she's grown in so many different ways. She's matured. She's gone through some real, real hardships and I think that the way that she's come back into the team this season, not only mentally but also physically, I think being away and back at home for over six months to come back in and be pretty much ready to go is a testament to her. The work that she wanted to put in and the work that she wants to do for her mum. As a friend, first and foremost, I'm really proud of her the way she's stepped up this season and I think she's got a massive career ahead of her.

on how to deal with players like Hinds when they’re not playing:RS: What we do to help players is we have a really strong set-up in our technical team so we work with all players have their personal development plans and all coaches have a group of four or five players that they work with both from a review perspective training, isolated repetition technical repetition check-ins in general so I think all players and Taylor specifically has had really good support challenge and support which is always important for us for our PDP coach going both directions me and Taylor have had quite some conversations throughout both in the difficult times but also like I said to her after the game the performance that she puts on the way she plays the way she communicates the way she does her actions with conviction for 90 minutes and it's been a while since she played 90 minutes that was going to be in the Champions League so much respect for that and that's her and together with other staff at the club with the performance team medical team making sure that she's ready to go at this moment in the north London derby you see with how much heart she played in that game she cares for Arsenal and this game was important to her and I think you could see it in the way she behaved on the pitch and she did amazing so I'm just really happy for her she played a big role for the team in that game and this definitely put her in a good position going forward as well excellent.

on the understanding between Russo and Stanway:AR: Georgia was my first friend on England camp when we were about 13, so I think we've played together for a really long time. I understand what she's trying to do on the pitch and she understands me too, so I think there's a natural connection there. Again, someone I've played with for a really long time, so I think that's great and nice that it came off in the north London derby but yeah we work on a lot of things, especially when I'm a little bit deeper in that role and we're more closely connected, so yeah, she finds me in spaces that I know she'll give me the ball and vice versa so it was really nice to get that combination and she's a player that I love playing with.

on transitioning between the number 10 and number nine roles:AR: I feel like I've done it a lot more now, so it becomes a lot easier than it did at the start. I understand the role in and out of possession and I have good conversations with Renée and Aaron, who does the out-of-possession stuff too, so the role's really clear. I think a lot of the work that I do in the 9 is often a little bit deeper, so it has a lot of similarities with the number 10 position. I think ultimately I want to be scoring and creating as much as I can and I think you can do that both in the 9 and the 10 and we have great players that can play all over the front four, so I think it's just about how we can connect, how we can set up best opportunities for each other and play ourselves and each other into their strengths.

on helping Hinds to be prepared for minutes:AR: Something that I would say to a lot of the girls is that you always have to be ready. Football changes so fast and you're always going to be needed. We've seen that last year with players when they step up and they do great, so I think for Taylor it was about making sure that I'm there for her, if there's anything that she needed but making sure that I kept her ready and kept her mindset focused on when she gets an opportunity, she will take it and she did that. She stepped up and she knows we have so much quality in our squad and Taylor included. She got a chance and she did really great and I think that's credit to us and the team to have players that are so ready to step in and commit to the team and commit to what we're trying to build. So yeah, it was really nice to see.

on if she’s tempted to keep consistency in the line-up to build momentum:RS: That's always an important factor in how I think we start the game and finish the game. So again, for this one, we're looking at which 11 players we think are best for us to start but then we also know, with the Benfica opponent, that the way their games have played out, finishing is really important as well, so you have sharpness and quality and injections to finish the game. Trying to find the right balance there but yeah, of course consistency is an important one: freshness, readiness, short turnarounds, so that all plays in plus a million of other factors. We think we're in a good place for how we want to start and finish for tomorrow.

on if it’s good to have this game so soon after the derby win:RS: Absolutely, I think we love it and the players love it. Playing so many games, that's why here at Arsenal we want to compete, play our games. That's the best, we look forward to Meadow Park, the closest to the fans. Champions League is always special. Special nights for the fans. How they were during the game and after the game was incredible. They're the best, so that moment afterwards we knew how important it was for us but also for the fans to get the win against Tottenham. I was really happy we could reward them for their resilience as well, so we look forward to the game tomorrow.

on having a difficult run of form before the win against Spurs:AR: Of course, it's frustrating. We're all elite athletes, around elite sport and we want to win every single game but football doesn't always work like that. We've kind of just kept it simple, stripped things back and focused on the basics in training. Sometimes when things don't go your way, you can begin to overcomplicate and overanalyse and look too deeply into things. I think that's the last thing we've done. We've tried to just stay calm, stay free and focus on what we're good at and I think that's what we saw in the north London derby, we saw everyone playing with grit, playing with passion and hopefully we'll continue that going into Benfica tomorrow.

on if we feel different this week off the back of that win:AR: It was nice to win, especially the north London derby. I think we know what that means to this club and the history of this team, it's a game every season that we look forward to and we want to give to the fans. I don't think it matters who we play. We now know that that's the standard, that's the level of grit and togetherness that we show on the pitch and that's the standard. Renée's message for the game is that now we need to go and back it up and that's on us as players tomorrow, going out there against Benfica.

items.summaryZh: 斯勒格斯与鲁索出席赛前发布会，展望对阵本菲卡比赛。
bodyZh: 雷妮·斯勒格斯和阿莱西亚·鲁索于周二在索布哈地产训练基地出席了对阵本菲卡比赛前的媒体新闻发布会。
两人展望了周三在博勒姆伍德梅多公园球场进行的欧洲女足冠军联赛较量。
以下是她们就以下话题所说的一切……
关于北伦敦德比之后的这两天：RS：感觉很好。球员和工作人员在赛后第二天放假一天。我想你可以从赛后的庆祝活动中看出这对我们有多好，以及它所产生的能量。我们已经回来了，所以这是一种平衡，既要在赛后恢复，又要为明天的本菲卡比赛做准备。而且能量很棒。
关于享受点球和庆祝活动：AR：是的，真的很好。我认为你可以从我们的比赛方式以及最后庆祝的方式中看出，赢得北伦敦德比对我们意义重大。这对俱乐部、我们球员和工作人员都意义重大。所以，能够取得这场胜利感觉真的很棒，我们希望现在这能为接下来的几场比赛建立势头。
关于里德和阿吉曼的伤情：RS：她们还没有回归，情况和上一场比赛一样。弗里达的恢复进展也很顺利，但明天复出还为时过早。金·利特尔已重返大名单。
关于凯蒂是否遇到困难：RS：我们拭目以待。她当然是从长期伤病中恢复过来。所以希望一切都好，我们会做一些评估。

关于卡特利和海因斯搭档是否是长期解决方案：RS：我认为她们在比赛中表现得极其出色。我认为比赛的进程正如我们所愿，功劳归于球场上的球员，她们做得非常对，以如此坚定的信念和高质量完成了各自的角色。所以我认为左路尤其有一场非常精彩的比赛，但作为整体，我认为我们以强度、战斗精神以及北伦敦德比所需的坚韧进行比赛的方式，这就是我们的基础。这也是未来表现的基础。有一些非常好的事情，但现在我们必须用表现来支持它，下一场比赛就是明天。

关于随着时钟拨回我们的整体情绪是否发生了变化，以及我们是否是逐场进行而不是逐场看来着：RS：依然是逐场进行。我想我的孩子还没习惯时间的变化！顺便说一句，今天早上在下雨。当我们在训练场上时，天气很好而且阳光灿烂。不，我们坚持一场一场来。这对我们很重要。我们不会看太远。我们对明天的欧冠比赛感到非常兴奋。很高兴能回到梅多公园球场与球迷拉近距离，并在灯光下踢球。我知道踢欧冠对球员意味着什么，所以要一场一场来，下一场是对阵本菲卡。
关于对阵热刺是否是对阵本菲卡的良好演练：RS：我们预计会有一些相似之处。我认为北伦敦德比中的拼抢次数、球场上的身体对抗、球场上战斗所需的强度，我们预计明天也会如此。他们是一支非常强悍的球队，有着良好的组织、良好的结构和拼搏精神。从这个意义上说，我们预计会遇到类似的情况。好消息是我们周末的比赛做得很好，我们想把它提升到下一个水平。

关于金球奖：AR：是的，真的很好。我认为庆祝人们的赛季并将足球世界聚集在一起是很特别的。和马里奥娜一起去很好。是的，我认为这是一个你可以享受足球高潮和低谷的时刻。我认为看到哈里·凯恩获胜是一个特别的夜晚。我对此感到非常兴奋。我认为他是我的榜样之一，我想一旦宣布，我就起鸡皮疙瘩了。显然，阿莱克西亚·普特利亚斯也是一名出色的球员，所以我认为庆祝他们个人的时刻真的很好。然后我也认为这给了你一些继续前进的动力。我知道我们今年作为一支球队想要取得什么成就，也许一开始很艰难，但我相信这支球队和这个赛季未来依然有伟大的事情等待着我们。
关于她是否像凯恩一样突破状态的低谷：AR：我的意思是，说我像哈里·凯恩是一种荣幸，但我认为我绝对会向他学习。我认为他是一位杰出的领袖和球员。我喜欢他如何稍微回撤得更深一点，他接到传中，找到半码射门的空间，他双脚都很出色。所以，是的，如果有什么人的比赛我可以尝试学习的话，那就是他的。
关于我们本赛季是否需要在心态上更加坚韧：AR：百分之百。我认为你在整个赛季中总会学到不同的东西。你面临着不同的挑战，我想，是的，你必须深入挖掘。我认为，当然，这段时间有点艰难，但我们有一支坚韧的球队，周围有坚韧的人，我认为有时艰难的时刻会激发出球队非常棒的东西，我希望这也是我们本赛季将要继续做的事情。

关于战胜热刺后我们想看到更多什么：RS：是的，就像我刚才说的，我们取胜的基础是我们带给比赛的强度，我们作为一个整体共同进攻和防守、战斗、坚韧、恢复力，因为他们也打进了比赛的第一球，我们必须从中恢复过来。所以这些对我们很重要，我们绝对希望把这些带到明天晚上的比赛中。我认为我们进球的那次进攻，阿莱西亚为乔治亚创造了机会，我们如何进行多次深度的跑动，我认为这是我们第三次或第四次通过跑动打破防线，然后我们非常镇定地将球传给面向前方的球员并完成射门。这非常积极，也是我们一直在努力讨论的事情。所以如果我们能更频繁地做到这一点并更一致地将这一点带入比赛，我们就知道阵容中的实力。但是的，基础绝对在于坚韧和战斗。
关于现在是否更强调欧冠的成功：RS：尽管开局对我们来说很艰难，而且有些结果我们并不满意，但我仍然认为现在下结论还为时过早，因为联赛中还有很多比赛要打。所以就像我刚才说的，我们要一场一场来，我们为再次成为欧冠的一员感到非常自豪。这是一个 fantastisch 的舞台，这就是我们所关注的，所以明天对阵本菲卡。

关于我们在战术上如何应对本菲卡：RS：当然，他们有自己的特点。还记得我们去年去那里打的客场比赛吗，他们给我们制造了困难，我们最终2-0赢了。他们已经对阵过尤文图斯和拜仁。他们有竞争力，我们知道他们明天也会和我们竞争。所以会有一些相似之处。他们有自己的特点，在联赛中有着非常强悍、紧凑的结构。我想自2024年以来他们有过惊人的连胜。因此，根据我们与他们进行的上一场比赛，有很多相似之处，但他们做的事情略有不同。一些人员也不同。

关于前锋错失良机后如何重置：AR：首先也是最重要的是，关于训练。我们在训练中经常练习射门时刻以及点球。所以我想每当那一周的时刻到来时，你知道你已经在这一周做好了工作，这给了我信心。此外，我认为这就是足球的运作方式。作为一名中锋、一名攻击手，你知道你会得到机会，关键是尽你所能做到最好。我觉得那是一次不错的接触，是一次不错的扑救（利兹·科普在下半场初期的扑救）。我在罚点球时没有感到太大压力。显然，我知道我想为俱乐部进球，因为这在当时意味着什么，但你一直在为这些时刻进行训练，所以它训练你在这些时刻做好准备。

关于我们能否从上赛季客场2-0战胜本菲卡的比赛中吸取任何经验：AR：是的，就像雷妮说的，我们知道他们是一支非常难缠的球队。当我们客场对阵他们时，我们看到了这一点。当他们对阵拜仁时，我们看到了这一点，直到比赛快结束时他们才进球，而且我认为我们什么时候进球并不重要。当然，我们希望在前几分钟进球，但有时足球并不是这样的。所以我们做好了准备，我们会尽一切可能尽早打破他们的防线，但我们也知道他们有威胁，我们也必须意识到这一点。所以是的，带着信心进入比赛，无论它是在第一分钟还是最后一分钟，无论如何我们都专注于胜利。

关于作为队长在困难时刻做什么：AR：我们有一支充满年轻天才的阵容，同时也有在顶级赛事中效力很长时间的非常有经验的职业球员，我觉得我正在慢慢向那个方向靠拢，所以我有责任多站出来一点。我认为我的领导方式是通过我的训练以及我在球场上的付出。这是我每天都承诺的事情。但同时，我是一个非常积极、随和的人，所以我想有时当对结果有很大压力且处于困难时期时，这可以帮助年轻球员。也许我认为我可以尝试减轻他们的一些压力，这是我引以为豪的事情。作为一名队长，我仍在学习。我有很棒的人可以仰望。我认为我通过做自己并保持真实来尽我所能地帮助他们，希望我能在这个角色中继续成长。

关于科尼-克罗斯本赛季的状态：AR：我四年前签约认识的基拉与现在完全是不同的人和球员。我认为她在很多不同的方面都有所成长。她成熟了。她经历了一些真正非常非常艰难的时期，我认为她本赛季重返球队的方式，不仅在精神上而且在身体上，离开并回到家乡六个月多，然后回来几乎随时准备上场，这对她来说是一个证明。她想要投入的工作以及她想为她妈妈做的工作。首先作为朋友，我为她本赛季的出色表现感到非常自豪，我认为她前途无量。

关于如何处理像海因斯这样没有上场时间的球员：RS：我们为了帮助球员所做的是，我们在技术团队中拥有一个非常强大的架构，因此我们与所有球员合作，制定她们的个人发展计划，所有教练都有一组四到五名球员，他们与她们合作，包括从复盘角度、训练、孤立重复训练、技术重复训练、一般签到，所以我认为所有球员，特别是泰勒，都得到了非常好的挑战和支持，这对我们的PDP教练双向沟通来说总是很重要的，我和泰勒在困难时期进行了很多对话，但就像我在赛后对她说的那样，她展现出的表现、她踢球的方式、她沟通的方式、她以90分钟的坚定信念完成动作的方式，而且她已经有一段时间没有踢满90分钟了，那将是在欧冠中，所以非常尊重这一点，这就是她，与俱乐部其他绩效团队、医疗团队的员工一起，确保她在这个时刻的北伦敦德比中准备好上场，你看到她在那场比赛中踢球是多么用心，她在乎阿森纳，这场比赛对她很重要，我想你可以从她在球场上的表现中看出这一点，她做得太棒了，所以我真的为她感到高兴，她在球队的那场比赛中发挥了重要作用，这绝对也为她接下来的发展奠定了良好的基础。

关于鲁索和斯坦威之间的默契：AR：当我们大约13岁时，乔治亚是我在英格兰训练营的第一个朋友，所以我想我们一起踢了很长时间的球。我明白她在球场上试图做什么，她也明白我，所以我想有一种自然的联系。同样，我和她一起踢球很长时间了，所以我想这很好，很高兴它在北伦敦德比中实现了，但是的，我们有很多事情要合作，特别是当我稍微回撤到那个角色并且我们联系更紧密时，所以是的，她会在我知道她会把球传给我的空间找到我，反之亦然，所以能够实现这种配合真的很好，她是我喜欢和她一起踢球的球员。

关于10号和9号角色之间的转换：AR：我觉得我现在做得更多了，所以比刚开始时容易多了。我理解有球和无球时的角色，我和雷妮以及负责无球战术的亚伦进行了很好的交流，所以这个角色非常明确。我认为我在9号位所做的很多工作通常稍微深入一些，所以它与10号位有很多相似之处。我认为最终我想尽可能多地进球和创造机会，我认为你在9号位和10号位都可以做到这一点，我们有出色的球员可以踢前场四人的任何位置，所以这只是关于我们如何联系，如何为彼此创造最佳机会，以及如何发挥我们和彼此的优势。

关于帮助海因斯为上场时间做好准备：AR：我对很多女孩说的一件事是，你必须随时准备好。足球变化太快了，你随时都会被需要。我们在去年看到球员们站出来表现出色，所以我想对泰勒来说，确保我在她身边，如果有任何她需要的，但要确保我让她保持准备好，让她的心态专注于当她有机会时，她会抓住它，她做到了。她站了出来，她知道我们阵容中有如此多的实力，包括泰勒在内。她得到了机会，她做得非常好，我认为这要归功于我们和团队，拥有能够随时站出来并致力于团队以及致力于我们正在努力建立的愿景的球员。所以是的，看到这一幕真的很好。

关于她是否倾向于保持阵容的一致性以建立势头：RS：这始终是我们认为如何开始比赛和结束比赛的重要因素。所以再次对于这场比赛，我们正在研究我们认为最适合我们首发的11名球员，但我们也知道，对于本菲卡这个对手，根据他们比赛的进行方式，收尾也非常重要，所以你要保持敏锐度、质量和活力来结束比赛。试图在其中找到正确的平衡，但是的，当然一致性是一个重要因素：新鲜感、准备就绪、短间歇，所有这些加上数百万的其他因素都在起作用。我们认为我们在明天的首发和收尾方式上处于一个很好的位置。

关于在德比取胜后不久进行这场比赛是否很好：RS：绝对是的，我想我们很喜欢，球员们也很喜欢。踢这么多比赛，这就是为什么我们在阿森纳想要竞争、踢我们的比赛。那是最好的，我们期待梅多公园，最接近球迷的地方。欧冠总是特别的。对球迷来说是特别的夜晚。他们在比赛中和比赛后的表现令人难以置信。他们是最好的，所以在随后的那一刻，我们知道这对我们以及对球迷来说击败托特纳姆热刺有多么重要。我真的很高兴我们也能回报他们的坚韧，所以我们期待明天的比赛。

关于在战胜热刺之前经历了一段艰难的状态：AR：当然，这令人沮丧。我们都是精英运动员，身处精英体育环境中，我们想赢得每一场比赛，但足球并不总是那样运作的。我们只是保持简单，剥离复杂的事情，专注于训练中的基础。有时当事情不如你所愿时，你可能会开始过度复杂化、过度分析并深入研究事情。我想这是我们最不应该做的事情。我们试图保持冷静，保持自由，专注于我们擅长的东西，我想这就是我们在北伦敦德比中看到的，我们看到每个人都带着坚韧、带着激情在踢球，希望我们将带着这种状态继续迎接明天对阵本菲卡的比赛。

关于在这场胜利之后我们本周的感觉是否有所不同：AR: 能够取胜感觉很好，尤其是北伦敦德比。我想我们知道这对这家俱乐部和这支球队的历史意味着什么，这是我们每个赛季都期待的比赛，我们想把它献给球迷。我认为我们和谁比赛并不重要。我们现在知道这就是标准，这就是我们在球场上表现出的坚韧和团结水平，这就是标准。雷妮对这场比赛的信息是，现在我们需要去支持它，这取决于我们作为球员明天在对阵本菲卡的比赛中走上球场。

items.titleEn: U21s preview: AFC Wimbledon v Arsenal
items.summaryEn: We face the League One side looking to progress to the knockout stages of the EFL Trophy
bodyEn: Our under-21s take on AFC Wimbledon on Tuesday evening (6pm UK) looking to progress to the knockout stages of the EFL Trophy for the first time.
After defeat to Barnet in our opening game in the group stages, we battled to a deserved 2-1 win over Leyton Orient, meaning we enter the final round of fixtures second in Southern Group F.

Three points in tonight's contest would see us make it through to the last 32, while a win on penalties would leave us waiting for Leyton Orient's result against Barnet on Tuesday, November 10 to discover our fate.
EARLY FORM FADES FOR DONS
After a promising start to the season, Wimbledon have hit something of a rut in October.
The Dons are without a win since a 1-0 success against Doncaster Rovers on September 12, going seven games without a victory in all competitions since.

Both matches in the EFL Trophy have ended in defeat for the south London side, although they do have two points on the board. Wimbledon took both Barnet and Leyton Orient to penalties, but were beaten on spot kicks by both opponents.
Wimbledon's only hope of progressing to the knockout stages is to beat us at the Cherry Red Records Stadium and hope that Leyton Orient don't beat Barnet by a bigger margin.
HOW TO FOLLOW
Matches in the EFL Trophy are available to watch on Sky Sports + for viewers in the UK.

Live updates will also be available before, during and after the game on our Academy X channel. Post-match, don't miss an exclusive interview with our Academy head coach David Horseman, as well as highlights of all the key action from south London.

items.titleZh: U21前瞻：AFC温布尔登对阵阿森纳
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳U21客场对阵AFC温布尔登，力争晋级EFL奖杯赛淘汰赛。
bodyZh: 我们的U21青年队将于周二晚间（英国时间晚上6点）对阵AFC温布尔登，力争首次晋级EFL奖杯赛的淘汰赛阶段。
在小组赛首战不敌巴尼特后，我们以2-1的比分力克莱顿东方，这使得我们在进入最后一轮比赛时排名南部F组第二。
今晚的比赛全取三分将确保我们晋级三十二强，而点球取胜则需要等待莱顿东方在11月10日对阵巴尼特的比赛结果来决定我们的命运。
对手近期状态下滑
在赛季开局表现不错之后，温布尔登在十月份陷入了低谷。
自9月12日以1-0战胜唐卡斯特流浪者之后，温布尔登已经各项赛事七场不胜。
这家南伦敦球会在EFL奖杯赛的两场比赛均告负，不过他们目前积两分。温布尔登在对阵巴尼特和莱顿东方时都将比赛拖入了点球大战，但均在点球决战中落败。
温布尔登晋级淘汰赛的唯一希望是在樱桃红唱片球场击败我们，并寄希望于莱顿东方击败巴尼特的净胜球优势不大。
如何观看直播
英国观众可以通过Sky Sports +观看EFL奖杯赛的比赛。
我们的Academy X频道也将在赛前、赛后以及比赛期间提供实时动态更新。赛后不要错过对我们青训主教练戴维·霍斯曼的独家采访，以及来自南伦敦所有关键动作的精彩集锦。

bodyEn: The headlines around Fleetwood Town are rarely about what happens on the pitch. Noteworthy elements include Jamie Vardy’s celebrated status as a former player, a partnership signed with a team in Uzbekistan and the owner Andrew Pilley resigning in 2023 after being convicted of fraud, for which he was jailed for 13 years. There is often something noteworthy going on in relation to the Fylde coast club.

It is no different this week, although this time football is taking centre stage as Arsenal head to Highbury Stadium on Tuesday for a Carabao Cup fourth-round tie against the League Two side. There is no link to the Gunners’ former home in Islington and the ground is a world away from what the visitors are used to, its capacity a fraction of the Emirates Stadium. The Championship side Sheffield United were deservedly beaten there in the previous round, unable to cope with their opponents or the conditions, but the Cod Army anticipate a sterner test from Mikel Arteta’s aristocrats.

Even against the Blades, the ground was less than half full but Tuesday will bring the venue’s biggest football attendance; the only other time it has sold out was for a fireworks display. The capacity is 5,300 and the stadium has four parking spaces, leaving Arsenal representatives to find alternatives on the street.

Fleetwood have a loyal local fanbase and occasions such as this can aid growth. Since the draw they have sold about an extra 200 season tickets to supporters keen to guarantee a place at the best show in town.

“It’s definitely the biggest game we’ve hosted, the Premier League champions at Highbury,” the club legend and assistant coach Nathan Pond says. “I think it’s just going to be a special night for everyone involved at the club.”

Pilley was the driving and financial force behind the club’s rise from non-league to a decade in League One, from which they were relegated in 2024. He handed the reins to his son Jamie, and some feel Pilley Sr’s absence has left a hole.

Away from high-profile managers including Uwe Rösler, Graham Alexander, Charlie Adam, Scott Brown and Joey Barton, a long-term project was growing in the background. Rösler and Barton were close to leading Fleetwood into the Championship, losing play-off semi-finals in 2016-17 and 2019-20 respectively. Defeat at Exeter last Saturday left the club 18th in League Two.

Matt Lawlor, the head coach since January, is an under‑the‑radar figure considering the names of some of his predecessors. He is a local who spent his playing career in non-league, representing Bamber Bridge for much of it. Lawlor has progressed from hard‑as-nails midfielder to impressive coach, spending time working for Manchester United’s foundation before joining Fleetwood’s respected academy. Regarded as a firefighter, he took charge for caretaker/interim spells at Fleetwood and their Irish sister club, Waterford, in between being part of the staff under Adam and Pete Wild, whom he succeeded.

At academy level, the club is aiding the careers of players and coaches. Bournemouth’s James Hill came through the ranks and the sale of Josh Feeney to Aston Villa in 2021 funded improvements that allowed the youth set-up to gain category two status. Three staff members have moved to Premier League clubs in recent months.

Fleetwood tried to establish global links beyond Waterford. In 2015, they announced their short‑lived partnership with Lokomotiv Tashkent, as part of which players were invited from Uzbekistan to Fleetwood for trial. They founded Fleetwood United in Dubai in 2021 but sold the club in 2024.
In South Africa they created Western Cape Fleetwood Football Club in 2021 and partnered with Hout Bay United Football Community a year later but are no longer involved with either project.

Fleetwood’s training ground, opened by Sir Alex Ferguson in 2016, is regarded as one of the best facilities in the EFL. The club make money from hosting touring youth teams there, as part of which matches against local academy and grassroots teams – including Fleetwood’s – are offered.

The training ground is open to the public, meaning fans can sit at the cafe and take in a session before chatting with the players about all and sundry, but mainly football. “The fans do come down quite a lot and interact with staff and players, which I think is important for a community football club like ourselves,” Pond says.

“There’s no barriers between us. I think that’s really important for the club we’ve come from, to maintain those things. Some of the loyal fans who come down to the training ground every now and then and go to every game, they’ve got an understanding and they’ve had conversations with the players. After a bad result, there’s no malice in it because they know the character of the lads.”

Being on a peninsula could make conditions interesting for Arsenal, with wind and rain predicted in the wake of Storm Boelo. “You can play the first half [against] the wind, come out for the second half and still be against it,” Pond says. “It goes in all directions.”
Pond made 498 appearances for Fleetwood across seven divisions between 2003 and 2018 before returning to be part of the coaching staff. His teammates in the Conference Premier included Vardy.

“I meet people on the street, people who know I used to play for Fleetwood,” Pond says. “The first question they ask is: ‘Did you play with Vardy?’ Even on the Vardy documentaries, Fleetwood gets a mention. He’s put us in the limelight.”
They are back there, for one night at least.

items.titleZh: “风向四面八方”：弗利特伍德准备在海布里球场湿冷迎接阿森纳
items.summaryZh: 阿森纳将在联赛杯第四轮客场对阵英乙球队弗利特伍德，后者正迎来队史最大规模的主场比赛之一。
bodyZh: 围绕弗利特伍德镇的头条新闻很少与球场上的表现有关。值得注意的元素包括杰米·瓦尔迪作为前球员的知名身份、与乌兹别克斯坦一支球队签署的合作关系，以及老板安德鲁·皮利在2023年因欺诈罪被判入狱13年后辞职。关于这家位于菲尔德海岸的俱乐部，总有一些值得关注的事情发生。
本周也没有什么不同，尽管这一次足球成为了焦点，阿森纳将于周二前往海布里球场参加对阵这支英乙球队的联赛杯第四轮比赛。这与枪手此前在伊斯灵顿的旧主场没有任何关系，该球场与客队习惯的球场相去甚远，其容量只是酋长球场的一小部分。英冠球队谢菲尔德联队在上一轮比赛中在那里被当之无愧地击败，无法应对对手或场地条件，但“鳕鱼军团”预计米克尔·阿尔特塔的精英球队将带来更严峻的考验。
即使在对阵刀锋军团时，球场上座率也没有达到一半，但周二将带来该场地最大的足球上座率；它唯一一次门票售罄是举办烟花汇演。容量为5,300人，球场只有四个停车位，这让阿森纳代表不得不寻找街头替代方案。
弗利特伍德拥有忠实的本地球迷基础，这样的机会可以促进增长。自抽签以来，他们已经向热衷于保证在镇上最好演出中获得一席之地的支持者额外售出了大约200张季票。
“这绝对是我们主办过最大的一场比赛，英超冠军来到海布里，”俱乐部传奇人物兼助理教练内森·庞德说。“我认为对于俱乐部涉及的每个人来说，这将是一个特殊的夜晚。”
皮利是该俱乐部从非联赛崛起并在英甲度过十年的推动力和资金力量，他们于2024年降级。他将大权交给了他的儿子杰米，一些人认为老皮利的缺席留下了一个真空。
除了包括乌韦·罗斯勒、格雷厄姆·亚历山大、查理·亚当、斯科特·布朗和乔伊·巴顿在内的备受瞩目的主教练之外，一个长期项目正在幕后成长。罗斯勒和巴顿险些率领弗利特伍德升入英冠，分别在2016-17赛季和2019-20赛季的附加赛半决赛中失利。上周六客场负于埃克塞特后，该俱乐部在英乙联赛中排名第18位。
考虑到他的一些前任的名字，自1月以来担任主教练的马特·劳勒是一个低调的人物。他是一名当地人，职业生涯在非联赛度过，大部分时间代表班伯布里奇。劳勒从一名硬朗的中场球员成长为一名出色的教练，在加入弗利特伍德备受尊崇的青训营之前，曾在曼联基金会工作过。被视为一名救火队员，他曾在弗利特伍德及其爱尔兰姐妹俱乐部沃特福德担任看守/临时主帅，之后成为亚当和皮特·王尔德手下的工作人员，并接替了后者。
在青训层面，该俱乐部正在协助球员和教练的职业生涯。伯恩茅斯的詹姆斯·希尔是通过青训营培养出来的，2021年将乔什·费尼出售给阿斯顿维拉获得的资金资助了基础设施的改善，使青训体系获得了二级资格。最近几个月，三名员工已转投英超俱乐部。
弗利特伍德试图建立超越沃特福德的全球联系。2015年，他们宣布了与塔什干火车头的短命合作关系，作为其中的一部分，邀请了乌兹别克斯坦的球员前往弗利特伍德试训。他们于2021年在迪拜创立了弗利特伍德联队，但在2024年将其出售。
在南非，他们在2021年创建了西开普弗利特伍德足球俱乐部，并在一年后与豪特湾联足球社区合作，但不再参与这两个项目。
弗利特伍德的训练基地由阿历克斯·弗格森爵士于2016年启用，被认为是EFL最好的设施之一。该俱乐部通过在那里接待巡回青年队来赚钱，作为其中的一部分，他们提供与当地青训营和草根球队（包括弗利特伍德的球队）的比赛。

训练基地对公众开放，这意味着球迷可以坐在咖啡馆里观看训练，然后与球员聊聊各种事情，主要是足球。“球迷们确实经常来这里与员工和球员互动，我认为这对于像我们这样的小区足球俱乐部来说很重要，”庞德说。
“我们之间没有障碍。我认为这对于我们出身的俱乐部来说非常重要，能够保持这些东西。一些偶尔来到训练基地并观看每一场比赛的忠实球迷，他们有一种理解，并且与球员进行了对话。在糟糕的结果之后，里面没有恶意，因为他们了解小伙子们的性格。”
身处半岛可能会让阿森纳的比赛条件变得有趣，在博埃洛风暴之后，预计会有风雨。“你可以顶风踢上半场，下半场出来后依然是顶风，”庞德说。“风向是四面八方的。”
在2003年至2018年间，庞德在七个级别联赛中为弗利特伍德出场498次，之后回归成为教练组的一员。他在议会全国联赛中的队友包括瓦尔迪。
“我在街上遇到人，知道我曾为弗利特伍德效力的人，”庞德说。“他们问的第一个问题是：‘你和瓦尔迪一起踢过球吗？’即使在瓦尔迪的纪录片中，弗利特伍德也被提及。他让我们成为了聚光灯下的焦点。”
他们又回到了那里，至少度过一个夜晚。

The Cherries are smart at investing, far more so than Manchester United, who have wasted a lot of money by failing to look outside the box for players like Rayan, Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson. United may not have the wealth they previously showed in the transfer market but Bournemouth are showing what can be done within a budget and, more importantly, will be able to make a profit on signings. United, however, only know losses as everyone’s price tag diminishes the moment they come through the Old Trafford door. Jason Wilcox and others can point to certain factors that are against them but there are quality signings to be made at the right price if you have the ability to find them. Will Unwin
Match report: Manchester United 0-3 Bournemouth
Will Unwin: Carrick left carrying can for institutional failings

Aston Villa were quite happy to sell Emiliano Martínez but many feared it would be difficult to find an upgrade on the World Cup-winning goalkeeper. They have seemingly done so in the form of the £30m signing Zion Suzuki, who was superb against Manchester City. Nicolas Jackson’s goals stole the headlines but Suzuki’s bounty of saves ensured that Villa were victorious, while also impressing with his distribution. ”He’s ambitious. I think it’s very important, his mentality,” Unai Emery said. “Of course, we need a keeper first to save us in the goal, but as well we need one keeper to try to help us in our buildup. And in buildup, he’s a really fantastic player because he can play short, he can understand where is the superiority to break the opponent’s press. He has qualities to do long ball, getting our players in attack. So, we are very, very impressed how he adapted so quick with us.” WU
Match report: Aston Villa 2-1 Manchester City

Aside from the reaction to the half-time and full-time scores from Old Trafford, the biggest noise at Anfield was generated by Ronald Araújo showing no mercy in his challenges on Malick Yalcouyé and Charalampos Kostoulas. The on-loan Barcelona defender immediately endeared himself to the Kop with his commitment and quality, and was again in commanding form to help Andoni Iraola record his first Premier League home win as Liverpool head coach. “I think we all enjoyed watching Ronald fighting,” said Iraola. “He’s very good in the duels. Even the first goal, he wins two duels in a row and defensively he’s been really, really good. I’m happy for him because I’ve taken him out in the last two games because we needed more offensive things. But he has continued working with no issues and today we needed him more. He has given a very, very good 90 minutes.” Andy Hunter
Match report: Liverpool 2-0 Brighton

João Pedro is unlikely to make a swift return after picking up an injury in training. The Chelsea striker missed the defeat to Tottenham and had a scan on Sunday. Xabi Alonso did not sound optimistic after the Spurs game. The expectation is João Pedro will miss this week’s games against Liverpool and Manchester United as a minimum, leaving Alonso with problems in attack. It was strange he did not start Danny Welbeck against Spurs. Chelsea had no focal point and there are questions over their depth. Emmanuel Emegha, another struggling with injury, is yet to play since joining from Strasbourg. It is fair to wonder if selling Nicolas Jackson to Villa was the right move. Chelsea have played two league games without João Pedro this season and have lost both without scoring a goal. Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers are not as effective without him. Jacob Steinberg
Match report: Chelsea 0-2 Tottenham
Barney Ronay: Glitch in Chelsea’s coding costs Alonso while resurgent Spurs are all systems go

Mikel Arteta says he has been compiling a dossier of evidence of other managers straying outside the technical area after the Arsenal manager was shown a yellow card during the 2-0 win over Everton. It was his second of the season and leaves the Spaniard at risk of suspension if he gets one more, although Arteta suggested he is by no means the worst offender. “There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline – no yellows,” he said, naming no names. “I am clipping all of that so I now have a massive storage of images, so if somebody comes to me I can say: ‘I am not in the record yet.’ Somebody else has the record so let’s see. Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers. I don’t know what we are going to do – let’s see.” Ed Aarons
Match report: Arsenal 2-0 Everton

Nico González cost Manchester City £50m when they signed him early in 2025, as part of that January spree as Pep Guardiola tried to arrest the first real slump of his Premier League career. Although he started nine league games that season and 17 last, González made very little impact at the Etihad. He probably wasn’t even the best Nico González in world football, given the Argentinian winger’s performances for Juventus and Atlético. But the Spanish Nico González clearly is a player of substance, his calm in midfield one of the few undoubted positives for Newcastle so far this season. Only Lewis Hall has made more tackles per game than him, he set up Sven Botman’s goal at Coventry, while he’s made more key passes per game than anybody other than Harvey Barnes. At £48m, he may end up representing extremely good value. Jonathan Wilson

Match report: Crystal Palace 0-2 Newcastle

To ask a question that might be a segment on the Football Cliches podcast, is there a more “swirling litter” venue in the Premier League than the Stadium of Light? At this point it should be obvious this was not a classic. In part that is down the conditions – long balls ran away from players on both sides with frequency, and crisp packets were the only thing to trouble the nets at either end. Managing the Europa League was always going to be a challenge for Sunderland and returning from a midweek trip to Poland to earn a point against a team who have had a week to prepare is a good result, even if the Black Cats finish the weekend at the foot of the table. Tom Bassam
Match report: Sunderland 0-0 Leeds

In spectacular style, Oscar Bobb’s wait for a first Premier League goal for Fulham came to an end at Coventry. Bobb was signed in January, fitting the recruitment template that brought success and stability under Marco Silva, a manager adept at regenerating talent. Social media footage from the away end showed Fulham fans ask what Bobb, weaving and bobbing, was doing only for him to feint past two Coventry defenders and score. That broke the deadlock when Coventry appeared fully capable of claiming a point or better. It remains to be seen whether Álvaro Arbeloa possesses the some restorative powers as Silva. After two wins in succession, two clean sheets and a first win away from Craven Cottage since February, early-season panic has dissipated. For now. If survival is Fulham’s first objective, then successive wins over the promoted teams Hull and Coventry were minimum requirements. Though should Fulham aim much higher? Silva departed because his ambitions were not met. John Brewin
Match report: Coventry 0-1 Fulham

Brentford are still yet to win away from home in the league but are also unbeaten on their travels. The draws at Leeds, Bournemouth and Aston Villa can be considered decent results, but this goes in the missed opportunity pile. So far Hull have presented a stiffer challenge at MKM Stadium than predicted, but in terms of expectations for Brentford this fixture has more in common with playing Sunderland at home than it does with their previous draws on the road. Against Sunderland and at Hull, Keith Andrews’ side struggled when the onus was on the them to make the game. The Bees play like they would rather not have the ball. In this one, they had plenty of shots – 14 in total – but only Dango Ouattara and belatedly Jaidon Anthony truly troubled Konstantinos Tzolakis. Brentford need Igor Thiago firing again. TB
Match report: Hull 1-1 Brentford

With Nottingham Forest the Premier League’s joint-lowest scorers, the pressure on Liam Delap is increasing. At Ipswich, where he was a rare bright spot with 12 goals in the relegation season of 2024-25, Delap was booed on every touch. The jeers got louder when each of his four attempts on goal missed their target. Only three of 18 Premier League shots in a Forest shirt have been on target. The raw materials that Chelsea moved for in summer 2025 remain present, the physical prowess and ability to find promising positions. The finishing touches are, at present, lacking, when Forest need someone to start scoring. Failing to take their chances at Portman Road left Forest in the relegation zone, endangering Oliver Glasner, when the ownership is trigger-happy with managers. Chris Wood, previously Forest’s talisman, came on in the 89th minute for Delap, but has been no super-sub so far, without a goal or assist from seven cameo league appearances. JB
Match report: Ipswich 1-1 Nottingham Forest

items.summaryZh: 阿森纳主帅阿尔特塔因吃到黄牌收集证据，其他英超焦点还包括伯恩茅斯精明引援等。
bodyZh: 伯恩茅斯的这三名进球球员总共花费了8500万英镑，分别从瓦斯科达伽马、米德尔斯堡和波尔图加盟。樱桃军团在投资方面非常精明，远胜于曼联，曼联由于未能跳出常规思维去寻找雷恩、马库斯·塔弗尼尔和埃凡尼尔森这样的球员而浪费了大量金钱。曼联可能不再具备以往在转会市场上显露出的财力，但伯恩茅斯证明了如何在预算范围内做事，更重要的是，他们将能够从签约中获利。然而，曼联只知道亏损，因为每个人一踏入老特拉福德的大门，其身价就会贬值。贾森·威尔考克斯和其他人可以指出某些不利于他们的因素，但如果你有能力以合适的价格找到他们，转会市场上依然有优质的引援可做。威廉·昂温
比赛报告：曼联 0-3 伯恩茅斯
威廉·昂温：卡里克为体制上的失败背锅

阿斯顿维拉很乐意出售埃米利亚诺·马丁内斯，但许多人担心很难找到这位世界杯冠军门将的升级替代者。他们似乎通过以3000万英镑签下铃木彩艳做到了这一点，他在对阵曼城的比赛中表现出色。尼古拉斯·杰克逊的进球抢占了头条，但铃木彩艳的多次扑救确保了维拉的胜利，同时他的传球也让人印象深刻。“他很有雄心。我认为这非常重要，他的心态，”乌奈·埃梅里说道。“当然，我们首先需要一个能在门前拯救我们的门将，但同样我们需要一个能试图在进攻组织中帮助我们的门将。在组织进攻时，他真的是一个非常出色的球员，因为他可以短传，能够理解哪里有优势来打破对手的逼抢。他有能力送出长传，让我们的球员参与进攻。所以，对于他能如此迅速地适应我们，我们感到非常非常深刻的印象。”威廉·昂温
比赛报告：阿斯顿维拉 2-1 曼城

除了对老特拉福德半场和全场比分的反应外，安菲尔德最大的声浪是由罗纳德·阿劳霍在对阵马利克·亚尔库耶和哈拉兰波斯·科斯图拉斯的拼抢中毫不手软所引发的。这位租借自巴塞罗那的后卫以他的投入和实力迅速赢得了Kop看台的喜爱，并且再次展现出统治级的状态，帮助安多尼·伊劳拉取得了作为利物浦主教练的首场英超主场胜利。“我想我们都喜欢看罗纳德拼搏，”伊劳拉说。“他在争抢中非常出色。甚至在第一个球上，他连续赢下两次争抢，防守端他真的非常非常好。我为他感到高兴，因为我在前两场比赛中把他换下，因为我们需要更多进攻端的东西。但他毫无怨言地继续努力，今天我们需要他。他奉献了非常非常好的90分钟。”安迪·亨特
比赛报告：利物浦 2-0 布莱顿

若昂·佩德罗在训练中受伤后，不太可能迅速复出。这位切尔西前锋错过了对阵热刺的比赛，并在周日接受了扫描。哈维·阿隆索在热刺比赛后听起来并不乐观。预计若昂·佩德罗至少将错过本周对阵利物浦和曼联的比赛，这让阿隆索在进攻端遇到了麻烦。在对阵热刺时没有让丹尼·韦尔贝克首发出场显得有些奇怪。切尔西缺少进攻支点，他们的阵容深度也受到了质疑。埃曼努埃尔·埃梅加也是一名受困于伤病的球员，自从从斯特拉斯堡加盟以来尚未出场。人们不禁怀疑将尼古拉斯·杰克逊卖给维拉是否是正确的举动。切尔西本赛季在没有若昂·佩德罗的情况下踢了两场联赛且全部失利且未能进球。科尔·帕尔默和摩根·罗杰斯在没有他的情况下效率有所下降。雅各布·斯坦伯格
比赛报告：切尔西 0-2 热刺
巴尼·罗奈：切尔西代码中的漏洞让阿隆索付出代价，而复苏的热刺正全速前进

米克尔·阿尔特塔表示，在阿森纳2-0战胜埃弗顿的比赛中吃到黄牌后，他一直在收集其他教练离开指挥区的证据。这是他本赛季的第二张黄牌，如果再领一张，这位西班牙教练将面临禁赛的风险，尽管阿尔特塔暗示他绝不是违规最严重的。“有些教练在联赛中创下了纪录，10分钟内36次离开技术区——没有黄牌，”他说，没有点名任何人的姓名。“我正在剪辑所有这些画面，所以我现在有一个庞大的图像库，如果有人来找我，我可以（为自己辩护）。别人有这个纪录，让我们拭目以待。然后教练们在10分钟内领到36张黄牌。我不知道我们要怎么做——让我们拭目以待。”埃德·阿隆斯
比赛报告：阿森纳 2-0 埃弗顿

尼科·冈萨雷斯在2025年初加盟时花费了曼城5000万英镑，那是瓜试图遏制其英超执教生涯中第一次真正低谷的1月疯狂引援的一部分。尽管他在那个赛季首发了9场联赛，上赛季首发了17场，但冈萨雷斯在伊蒂哈德球场几乎没有什么影响。考虑到这位阿根廷边锋在尤文图斯和马德里竞技的表现，他可能甚至不是世界足坛最好的尼科·冈萨雷斯。但西班牙的尼科·冈萨雷斯显然是一个很有实力的球员，他在中场的冷静是纽卡斯尔本赛季至今少数几个毋庸置疑的积极因素之一。除了刘易斯·霍尔之外，他是队内场均铲球次数最多的球员，他在考文垂助攻了斯文·博特曼的进球，同时他场均关键传球次数比哈维·巴恩斯以外的任何人都多。以4800万英镑的价格，他最终可能会展现出极高的性价比。乔纳森·威尔逊

比赛报告：水晶宫 0-2 纽卡斯尔

抛出一个可能会成为《足球陈词滥调》播客中一个环节的问题：在英超联赛中，还有比光明球场更像“打旋垃圾”的场地吗？在这一点上，显而易见这并不是一场经典之战。部分原因归咎于比赛条件——双方的长传球经常滚出球员控制范围，包装袋是唯一能威胁到两端球网的东西。应对欧联杯对桑德兰来说一直是一个挑战，在周中远赴波兰客场归来后，从一支拥有一周备战时间的球队身上拿到一分是一个不错的的结果，即使黑猫军团在周末结束时积分榜垫底。汤姆·巴萨姆
比赛报告：桑德兰 0-0 利兹联

以一种 spectacular 的方式，奥斯卡·鲍勃等待首粒英超富勒姆进球的时刻在考文垂终结了。鲍勃于1月加盟，这符合在马尔科·席尔瓦带领下取得成功和稳定的引援模板，席尔瓦是一位擅长重塑天才的主教练。客场球迷看台上的社交媒体视频显示，富勒姆球迷还在询问扭动着身子的鲍勃在做什么，随后他就假动作晃过两名考文垂防守球员并破门得分。在考文垂似乎完全有能力全取三分或更好结果时，这打破了僵局。阿尔瓦罗·阿韦洛亚是否拥有像席尔瓦那样恢复球队生机的能力还有待观察。在取得两连胜、两场零封以及自2月以来的首个客场胜利后，赛季初的恐慌已经消散。暂时如此。如果保级是富勒姆的首要目标，那么连续战胜升班马赫尔城和考文垂是最低要求。不过富勒姆是否应该瞄准更高的目标？席尔瓦的离队正是因为他的雄心壮志未能得到满足。约翰·布鲁因
比赛报告：考文垂 0-1 富勒姆

布伦特福德在联赛中依然未能取得客场胜利，但客场保持不败。在利兹联、伯恩茅斯和阿斯顿维拉的平局可以被认为是体面的结果，但这将被归入错失良机的堆里。到目前为止，赫尔城在MKM球场的表现比预期的更具挑战性，但就布伦特福德的期望而言，这场比赛与主场对阵桑德兰有更多共同点，而不是他们之前在客场的平局。对阵桑德兰以及在赫尔城，基斯·安德鲁斯的球队在必须由他们主动发起进攻时陷入了挣扎。蜜蜂军团踢得好像他们宁愿不要球权。在这场比赛中，他们有很多射门——总共14次——但只有当古·瓦塔拉和随后的海登·安东尼真正对康斯坦丁诺斯·佐拉基斯制造了威胁。布伦特福德需要伊戈尔·蒂亚戈重新找回射门靴。TB
比赛报告：赫尔城 1-1 布伦特福德

由于诺丁汉森林是英超联赛中进球并列最少的球队之一，利亚姆·德拉普身上的压力正在增加。在伊普斯维奇，他曾是2024-25赛季降级区里的难得亮点并打入12球，但在那里德拉普每次触球都遭到嘘声。当他四次射门全部偏离目标时，嘘声变得更大。他在穿上森林球衣后的18次英超射门中只有3次射正。切尔西在2025年夏天看中他的身体素质和寻找有威胁位置的能力依然存在。终结能力目前有所欠缺，而森林正需要有人开始进球。在波特曼路未能把握住机会，使森林陷入降级区，并危及了对教练不耐烦的管理层。此前森林的护身符克里斯·伍德在第89分钟替补出场换下德拉普，但目前他还没有发挥超级替补的作用，在七次替补联赛出场中没有进球或助攻。JB

bodyEn: The wait goes on for David Moyes. The 63-year-old Scot must have been hoping that on his 14th visit to this stadium as Everton’s manager, his luck would change. Yet from the moment Ezri Konsa slammed home his first goal for Arsenal as the Premier League champions rediscovered their knack of scoring from set pieces, the writing was on the wall.

While it took until midway through the second half for Gabriel Magalhães to make sure of the victory, Arsenal were never going to let slip the chance of moving level on points at the top with Manchester City after their defeat by Aston Villa earlier in the day.

Asked whether it was strange that his side are again going toe-to-toe with their great rivals but with the added uncertainty of what punishment City will receive after being found guilty of 115 charges by the Premier League, Mikel Arteta said: “[We are] just focusing on what we can do. We are very pleased with 90% of the results and performances that we have.”

This was hardly a vintage performance from the clinical home side after a testing week but it did not need to be against opponents who offered precious little in attack, even if they defended for their lives at times.
Having gone six matches without defeat to start the season, a second in succession will only add to Everton’s concerns after confirmation that the club’s American owners want out.

“It was always going to be hard after conceding the early goal,” said Moyes, whose solitary victory at the Emirates was as West Ham’s manager in 2023. “I want us to challenge the top teams but it’s difficult when you see the strength of their bench.”

Everton’s record at this stadium is almost as bad as their manager’s. They arrived in north London having won twice in 35 matches here and had to do without Jarrad Branthwaite and Jack Grealish, who was ruled out with illness. It did not bode well for them when Arsenal took the lead in the seventh minute with a third corner in succession.

Gabriel made the crucial first contact at the near post and Jordan Pickford tipped the ball on to the crossbar, only for Vitaliy Mykolenko’s failed clearance under pressure from Viktor Gyökeres to allow Konsa to ram home from close range. After a record-breaking 25 goals from set pieces last season, it was their first of this campaign.
It was a measure of Arsenal’s exertions against Bayern Munich on Wednesday that Arteta rotated his side more than usual for a Premier League match, making five changes.

Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke spurned good opportunities to extend the lead in front of the watching England head coach, Thomas Tuchel. The latter was left out of the last squad, but could well benefit from Bukayo Saka’s expected long absence due to a thigh injury. He was inches away with an instinctive effort with his right foot from the edge of the area on the half-hour mark and was consistently Arsenal’s most dangerous threat.
Everton must have feared the worst as yet another Arsenal corner – 10 during the first half – was launched into the area. Yet the defence just about stood firm.

A moment’s lapse of concentration from Ben White just before half-time almost gave Everton an equaliser but Thierno Barry could not get enough on his attempt to flick the ball past David Raya in their clearest opening.
Gyökeres looked determined to make an impression on his first Premier League start of the season but the Sweden striker, who has yet to score for his club this term, looked laboured.

• With both Arsenal and Manchester City doing so this season, this is just the third top-flight campaign to have two teams win at least seven of their opening eight matches after 1892-93 (Preston and Sunderland) and 1913-14 (Blackburn and Manchester United).
• This was David Moyes’s 400th defeat across all competitions in his managerial career with all clubs. 31 of these have come against Arsenal, more than against any other opponent.
• The opener from Ezri Konsa (pictured celebrating) was Arsenal’s first set piece goal (excluding penalties) since May against Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one. Opta

He could not believe it when Tony Harrington penalised him for a foul on James Tarkowski and a sheepish Arteta earned himself a booking for protesting. Unsurprisingly, Gyökeres’ number was up soon after as Arsenal turned to their bench.
It took less than 60 seconds for Gabriel to head in at the back post as White offered Tuchel a timely reminder of his qualities with a brilliant cross.
Moyes’ frustration meant he joined Arteta in the referee’s notebook. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall could have made things interesting but his header fizzed just wide of a post.
Arsenal are now breathing down City’s necks, although whether this title race lasts the course remains unknown.

items.titleZh: 孔萨与加布里埃尔建功，阿森纳击败埃弗顿
items.summaryZh: 孔萨与加布里埃尔进球，阿森纳在主场击败埃弗顿。
bodyZh: 大卫·莫耶斯的等待还在继续。这位63岁的苏格兰人一定曾希望，在他作为埃弗顿主帅第14次做客这座球场时，自己的运气能有所改变。然而，当埃兹里·孔萨斩获他加盟阿森纳后的首粒进球，帮助这位英超卫冕冠军重新展现定位球得分能力的那一刻起，比赛的结局便已注定。
尽管直到下半场中段加布里埃尔·马加良斯才锁定胜局，但在曼城此前输给阿斯顿维拉之后，阿森纳绝不会错过这场积分追平领头羊的绝佳机会。
当被问及与老对手再次展开争夺是否有些奇怪，且曼城因被英超指控115项违规后面临何种处罚仍存不确定性时，米克尔·阿尔特塔表示：“我们只专注于我们能做的事情。对于90%的比赛结果和表现，我们都非常满意。”
经历了考验重重的一周后，表现高效的主队此役并非踢出了一场经典之战，但面对在进攻端几乎毫无建树、有时甚至拼死防守的对手，他们也无需踢得多么华丽。
在经历开局六场不败后，埃弗顿遭遇了连败，而在俱乐部美国老板寻求出售的确认传出后，这无疑会加剧球队的担忧。
“在过早丢球之后，比赛总是会变得异常艰难，”莫耶斯说道，他在酋长球场的唯一一场胜利还是2023年率领西汉姆联时取得的。“我希望我们能向顶级球队发起挑战，但看看他们替补席的厚度，这真的很困难。”
埃弗顿在这座球场的战绩几乎和他们主帅的客场战绩一样糟糕。他们来到北伦敦时带着在这里35场仅赢2场的纪录，并且缺少了扎拉德·布兰思韦特以及因病缺阵的杰克·格拉利什。当阿森纳在第7分钟利用连续第三个角球率先破门时，这对他们来说绝对不是什么好兆头。
加布里埃尔在近门柱抢到关键第一落点，皮克福德将球扑到横梁上，随后维塔利·米科连科在维克托·哲凯赖什的逼抢下解围失误，孔萨近距离推射破门。上赛季他们创纪录地打入25个定位球，这是他们本赛季的第一个定位球进球。
为了应对周三与拜仁慕尼黑的恶战，阿尔特塔本场在英超联赛中做出了比以往更多的轮换，首发阵容调整了五处。
在现场观战的英格兰主帅托马斯·图赫尔面前，埃贝雷奇·埃泽和农尼·马杜埃凯错失了扩大比分的良机。后者落选了上一期大名单，但很可能因布卡约·萨卡因大腿受伤预计将长期缺阵而受益。在上半场进行到第30分钟时，他用右脚在禁区边缘完成了一脚极具本能的射门，距离进球仅毫厘之差，并且自始至终都是阿森纳最具威胁的球员。
面对阿森纳在上半场罚出的第10个角球，埃弗顿一定感到凶多吉少。不过，他们的防线最终还是勉强守住了。
本·怀特在上半场结束前的一次注意力不集中几乎让埃弗顿扳平比分，但蒂尔诺·巴里在面对大卫·拉亚时没能充分完成推射，错失了他们全场最清晰的破门良机。
哲凯赖什似乎决心在本赛季他的首次英超首发出场中证明自己，但这位尚未在本赛季为俱乐部进球的瑞典前锋显得有些吃力。
随着阿森纳和曼城在本赛季均做到这一点，这是自1892-93赛季（普雷斯顿和桑德兰）以及1913-14赛季（布莱克本和曼联）以来，顶级联赛历史上第三次出现两支球队在开局前八场比赛中至少赢得七场的情况。
这是大卫·莫耶斯执教生涯各项赛事遭遇的第400场失利。其中有31场是对阵阿森纳，超过了他面对任何其他对手时的失利场次。
埃兹里·孔萨的闪击破门是阿森纳自5月对阵水晶宫以来打入的首个非点球定位球，从而结束了此前13场比赛定位球颗粒无收的尴尬纪录（数据来源：Opta）。
当主裁判托尼·哈灵顿判罚他对詹姆斯·塔科夫斯基犯规时，他简直不敢相信，而略显羞涩的阿尔特塔也因为抗议吃到了一张黄牌。不出所料，阿森纳随后便用替补球员换下了哲凯赖什。
仅仅用了不到60秒，加布里埃尔就在后点接怀特的精妙传中头球破门，怀特也借此再次及时向图赫尔展现了自己的能力。
莫耶斯的沮丧情绪让他在裁判的笔记本上也添上了名字。基兰·杜斯伯里-霍尔本有机会让比赛重现悬念，但他的头球擦着门柱偏出。
阿森纳目前正紧追曼城不放，尽管这场争冠大戏能否持续到最后目前仍未可知。
